India's primary health centres still run out of basic medicines like O R S, zinc and iron tablets, often while a clinic a few kilometres away has spare stock. AushadhiNet is an early warning and rebalancing system for public health supply chains, built on Google's stack and piloted on all seven hundred and sixty health facilities in Nashik district.

A district officer signs in and sees every facility on the map, coloured by how many medicines are close to running out. Teal is safe, amber means one medicine is short, and red means several. The officer drills down from the state, to the district, to a single facility.

For each medicine, the facility page shows current stock, next week's demand forecast with a range, and the probability of a stock out. The forecasting model is LightGBM trained on India's real H M I S health data, and on a held out test window it beats the naive baseline by nineteen percent.

Nurses don't need a new app. They report stock on WhatsApp, the way they already talk. O R S fifty is read and recorded instantly. When she misspells zinc, AushadhiNet is not sure, so it asks her to confirm before anything is written to the stock ledger. Nothing unconfirmed ever reaches the forecast.
It works in seven Indian languages. Switch to Marathi, and the nurse can report in her own script and her own digits. The replies, the confirmation, and the whole interface come back in Marathi.

When the forecast shows risk, an optimisation solver built on Google O R Tools proposes transfers from nearby facilities with surplus to facilities about to run dry. A human always decides. The officer approves, and both facilities are notified on WhatsApp.

Officers can also ask questions in plain language. The agent explains why a facility is at risk using the actual forecast. And it is guard railed: asked to ignore its rules and approve every order, it refuses. It can explain and draft, but it can never approve or send anything.
Finally, a public transparency view shows district level shortage totals, with no facility identifiers, so citizens can see the picture without exposing individual clinics.

In a replay on a synthetic Nashik ledger, rebalancing cut stock out weeks by six percent without adding any new supply. AushadhiNet: earlier warnings, smarter sharing, and people always in control. Thank you.
